Estimate a median lethal concentration

Source: R/lc50.R
lc50.Rd

Walks the EPA point-estimation flowchart, selects the method the manual directs for the data, runs it, and returns the estimate together with a record of how the method was chosen.

Usage

lc50(x, ..., p = c(1, 50), ci_level = 0.95, alpha = 0.05, method = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'tox_lc50'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'tox_lc50'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A tox_data() object, or a data frame that can be coerced to one by passing it through tox_data().

...

Additional arguments passed to tox_data() when x is a bare data frame, and otherwise unused.

p

The effect percentage or percentages to estimate, on a 1-99 scale. For example 25 requests an IC25, and 50 an LC50.

ci_level

Confidence level for interval estimates. Defaults to 0.95.

alpha

Significance level for the hypothesis tests themselves. The EPA manuals specify 0.05, one-sided.

method

Optional. Name of a method to use instead of the one the flowchart selects: one of "probit_lc", "spearman_karber", "trimmed_spearman_karber" or "graphical_lc50". Forcing a method warns and is recorded, as in tox_test().

object

A tox_lc50 object.

row.names

Unused.

optional

Unused.

Value

An object of class tox_lc50, a list with elements estimate (a tox_estimate), decisions, selected, overridden and data.

Details

The flowchart is Figure 6 of the acute manual. It branches on how many concentrations produced a partial response, on whether the probit model fits, and on whether the response runs the full way from none to complete. The four terminals are probit_lc(), spearman_karber(), trimmed_spearman_karber() and graphical_lc50().

Point estimation uses all the data. Unlike the hypothesis-testing branch, no concentration is excluded for complete response: section 9.5.2 of the chronic manual is explicit that concentrations dropped from the no-observed-effect concentration are retained here.

Functions

  • summary(tox_lc50): Print the decision trail above the estimate.

  • as.data.frame(tox_lc50): Return the estimates as a data frame.

References

US EPA (2002) EPA-821-R-02-012, Figure 6 and section 11.2.

Examples

# Acute Table 20, probit column: two partial responses and an adequate fit,
# so the flowchart selects the probit method.
fit <- lc50(
  acute_table20,
  response = "probit", n_exposed = "exposed", type = "quantal"
)
summary(fit)
#> EPA WET point estimate
#> Flowchart: EPA-821-R-02-012 Figure 6
#> 
#>    1  Are there two or more partial responses?
#>       2 -> 2 partial response(s)
#>       (EPA-821-R-02-012 Figure 6)
#>    2  Is the probit model appropriate?
#>       3.076 -> the probit model fits
#>       (EPA-821-R-02-012 Figure 6)
#>    3  Which method was used?
#>       Probit method
#>       (EPA-821-R-02-012 section 11.2.5)
#> 
#>  endpoint  p estimate   lower  upper                  ci_method
#>       LC1  1   7.9239  4.1468 10.959 Fieller on the log10 scale
#>      LC50 50  22.8720 18.7870 27.846 Fieller on the log10 scale
